_comment: An example to copy. Save your own as config.json, then check it with: python3 zelda_watch.py --check-config
_stores: Turn each store on or off. "on" checks it every 5 minutes, "off" skips it, and something like "every 30 minutes" or "every 2 hours" checks it less often, which makes a block less likely. A store left out of this list is off. Walmart and EB Games block GitHub's servers, so they are only checked from a home connection, even when on. Shops you add under custom_stores go in this list too.

notifications._people: Everyone who can get alerts. Topics are secrets and never go in this file: with one person, put the topic in the NTFY_TOPIC repository secret; with several, use one NTFY_TOPICS secret holding JSON such as {"me": "my-long-random-topic", "sam": "sams-topic"}.
notifications._status_alerts_to: Who gets the heartbeat, self-test results and 'watcher problem' warnings.
notifications._discord: Optional: post alerts to a Discord channel through a webhook (put its link in the DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL secret). A product's 'topic' pings the matching role. See README.md, 'Discord alerts'.

_custom_stores: Shops that are not built in. Anything on Shopify, and most shops that publish schema.org data, is read automatically. If --check-link says it cannot read a shop, add in_stock_text or sold_out_text: words the product page shows.
_products: Each product is a name plus its link at every store you would buy it from. Copy links straight from your browser. 'notify' is optional and defaults to everyone in notifications.people. A link can also be written as {"url": "...", "enabled": false} to pause it.
_heartbeat: Send a quiet all-clear this often (hours), so silence is trustworthy. Set to 0 to disable.

self_test._comment: Nintendo items that are normally in stock. The self-test checks these with the real checker and sends a real push, proving detection and delivery work. Only one needs to be in stock to pass.

discovery._comment: Optional: alert when new products matching these words appear on the Nintendo store, and start watching them. See README.md.
